description: Parallel Sessions, renewal, account binding, rotation, narrowing, and sign-out.

cases.description: A Session starts signed out: a DPoP token with expires_in > 0 (hours, not days), no scope, a session_id.
The same user runs two Sessions at once; each has its own session_id and both are served.
Renewing with session_id returns a new token for the same Session; the agent uses it from then on and the old one stops working.
Renewing another user's Session with this user's assertion is invalid_session.
A sign-in grants no more than the scopes requested and allowed for its type; partial consent shows in scope.
A sign-in asking for a scope the company does not offer is invalid_scope.
The Account Token signs a fresh signed-out Session in at the token endpoint.
After a refresh rotates the Account Token, the old one is invalid_grant; the new one works.
A refresh asking for fewer scopes gets a token with only those.
A refresh asking for a scope the Account Token does not hold is invalid_scope.
Another client_id presenting the Account Token gets invalid_grant.
An Account Token presented at an API as an access token is refused (invalid_token).
A Session signed in to one account refuses an Account Token for another: account_mismatch.
An Account Token used for another user's Session is invalid_session.
After revocation, the Session Token issued before it is handled as signed out on the next request (sign_in_required).
After revocation, renewal returns a signed-out token for the same Session, and the revoked token is invalid_grant.
Disconnecting the agent at the company revokes its Account Tokens and signs out its Sessions; the agent finds out from invalid_grant and sign_in_required.
A 429 carries Retry-After, and the SDK reports it without retrying early.
